title: Analysis of Mitochondrial Functions in Arthritis Patients' Synovial Membrane Samples
author: Péter ávor
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.buvcnw2w
materials: Intraoperatively harvested synovium biopsies are assessed with light microscopy and confocal imaging. Confocal imaging with a laser scanning endomicroscope (CLSM, FIVE1 system, Optiscan, Victoria, Australia) is started immediately after retrieving the synovial sample. The rigid confocal probe (excitation wavelength 488 nm; emission detected at 505–585 nm) is mounted on a specially designed metal frame and gently pressed onto the inner surface of the joint capsule (1 scan/image, 1024 x 512 pixels and 475 x 475 μm per image). For the in vivo staining, 0.01% acriflavine (Sigma-Aldrich, Budapest, Hungary) is applied topically [24]. The analysis is performed twice separately by the same investigator using a semiquantitative histology score (S0-S4) based on widening of synovial lining, neoangiogenesis, collagen fibre disorganization and fragmentation, as described previously [27]. For traditional light microscopy, the samples are fixed in buffered paraformaldehyde solution (4%) and embedded in paraffin. 5-μm thick sections are cut and then stained with haematoxylin and eosin (H&E).

Proinflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) and receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-beta ligand (RANKL) levels are measured in the synovial fluid samples using commercially available ELISA kit according to the manufacturer’s instruction (Sigma-Aldrich, Budapest, Hungary).

steps.title: Collect synovial samples
steps.instruction: Aspirate synovial fluid from the knee joint with an 18 G needle before incision and excise 1 × 1 cm synovium tissue pieces from the suprapatellar pouch while sparing Hoffa’s fat pad.

steps.title: Transport samples on ice
steps.instruction: Place fluid aliquots into Eppendorf tubes and keep on ice; place tissue pieces into 4 % (v/v) neutral‑buffered formalin for histopathology and into phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) for biochemical analyses, both kept on ice until processing.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue for respiration
steps.instruction: Homogenize each tissue sample in 200 µL MiR05 respiration medium using a glass Potter‑Elvehjem homogenizer.

steps.title: Load homogenate into O₂ chambers
steps.instruction: Weigh 50 µL of each homogenate into calibrated detection chambers set to a baseline oxygen concentration of 200 nmol mL⁻¹ in room air.

steps.title: Measure basal and substrate respiration
steps.instruction: Record steady‑state basal O₂ consumption, then add glutamate (10 mM) and malate (2 mM) to stimulate Complex I‑linked respiration; add succinate (10 mM) together with rotenone (0.5 µM) to assess Complex II‑linked baseline respiration; finally add ADP to a final concentration of 5 mM to determine oxidative phosphorylation capacity.

steps.title: Assess inner membrane integrity
steps.instruction: Add cytochrome C to a final concentration of 10 µM and monitor any increase in respiration as an indicator of inner mitochondrial membrane damage.

steps.title: Measure leak respiration
steps.instruction: Add the ATP synthase inhibitor oligomycin (1 mM) and record the resulting leak (LEAK) respiration.

steps.title: Determine maximal ETS capacity
steps.instruction: Add the protonophore FCCP to a final concentration of 0.5 µM and measure the uncoupled electron transport chain (ETC) coupling rate.

steps.title: Measure residual O₂ consumption
steps.instruction: Add rotenone (1 µM) and antimycin‑A (1 µM) to inhibit Complex I and III respectively, and record the residual oxygen consumption (ROX).

steps.title: Homogenize tissue for XOR assay
steps.instruction: Homogenize synovial membrane in phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) containing 50 mM Tris‑HCl, 0.1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM dithiothreitol, 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride, 10 µg mL⁻¹ soybean trypsin inhibitor, and 10 µg mL⁻¹ leupeptin.

steps.title: Centrifuge and ultrafilter XOR homogenate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 4 °C for 20 min at 24 000 g; transfer the supernatant to centrifugal concentrator tubes for ultrafiltration.

steps.title: Perform fluorometric XOR assay
steps.instruction: In the ultrafiltered supernatant, conduct a fluorometric kinetic assay measuring conversion of pterine to isoxanthopterine in the presence (total XOR) or absence (XO activity) of methylene blue as electron acceptor.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue for MPO assay
steps.instruction: Homogenize synovial tissue in 0.1 M Tris‑HCl buffer (pH 7.4) containing 0.1 M polymethylsulfonyl fluoride to inhibit proteases.

steps.title: Centrifuge MPO homogenate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the MPO homogenate at 4 °C for 20 min at 24 000 g.

steps.title: Measure MPO activity spectrophotometrically
steps.instruction: Measure myeloperoxidase activity of the supernatant at 450 nm using a UV‑1601 spectrophotometer (Shimadzu, Japan) and express results relative to protein content.

steps.title: Prepare fluid for nitrotyrosine ELISA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge synovial fluid at 15 000 g, collect the supernatant, and keep on ice until assay.

steps.title: Perform nitrotyrosine ELISA
steps.instruction: Incubate supernatants overnight in precoated (mouse anti‑rabbit IgG) microplates with anti‑nitrotyrosine rabbit IgG and nitrotyrosine acetylcholinesterase tracer; develop with Ellman’s reagent and read absorbance; normalize nitrotyrosine content to protein and express as ng mg⁻¹.
